why.text: The challenge requires replacing fixed-threshold rules with a machine learning visual defect classifier that generalises across seasons (C999-CH1).

Stojanović co-authored work on few-shot learning for surface defect detection on reflective metal parts using prototypical networks (SYN-PUB-06388) and on anomaly detection in multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning (SYN-PUB-06391).
Stojanović co-authored work on domain randomisation for cross-domain transfer in visual defect detection across different material types and manufacturing processes (SYN-PUB-06393).

The VISIONQC project develops modular AI-powered inspection platforms for SME manufacturers with minimal labeled data requirements and includes pilot deployments at regional manufacturing SMEs (SYN-PRJ-0011).

problem.text: Stojanović and the company would train and validate a deep learning defect classifier on the 40,000 labeled apple images (C999-CH1), applying domain randomisation and cross-domain transfer techniques (SYN-PUB-06393) to handle seasonal appearance variation, and using active learning (SYN-PUB-06396) to prioritise re-annotation of the hardest bark-damage and early-rot cases, with the goal of exceeding the current ~88% accuracy on the deployed sorting line.

risks.text: All cited defect detection work covers industrial metal and assembly-line components; no publication covers organic produce or food-surface texture, so the class-overlap characteristics specific to bark damage and rot may require additional domain work.

The active learning framework (SYN-PUB-06396) is validated with industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-moulded plastic components; the record does not cover multi-season labeled datasets of organic produce.
